analytical_models.equation_role: γ_SFE = 2ρΔG^γ→ε + 2σ, where ρ is the molar surface density along {111} planes, ΔG^γ→ε is the molar Gibbs energy of the γ→ε transformation, and σ is the interfacial energy per unit area of the γ/ε boundary
analytical_models.model_note: The calculated γ_SFE for 4Al_γ (23 °C) is 51.25 mJ·m^-2 (Table 2).

parameters.name: σ (interfacial energy per unit area of γ/ε boundary)

computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Thermodynamic functions and parameters listed in literature [35]
computational_details.simulation_method: Thermodynamic calculation of stacking fault energy (γ_SFE)

analytical_models.equation_role: σ(γ)(ε) = K_SB M_SB G b/D + 0.8 K_DCB M_DCB G b/D + 0.2 K_DC M_DC G b/D, with M_SB = M_DCB = 3.06, M = 2.44, G = 70 GPa, b = 0.25 nm
analytical_models.model_note: Fig. 9(a) uses the average slip band spacing, dislocation cell block size and dislocation cell size of 4Al austenite steel to derive K_SB+DCB = 2.03 and K_DC = 2.02.

computational_details.simulation_method: Empirical similitude-coefficient (K) determination from the plastic-flow relationship (τ-τ0)/G = K b/D
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The obtained K values are close to reported K of 2.0-2.9 for austenitic stainless steel [63,64]; the similarity constant of austenite in 8Al steel is approximated by that in 4Al steel.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Four ingots with nominal compositions of Fe-35Mn-xAl-1C-0.1Nb-0.1V-1Mo-1W (x = 4, 6, 8, 10 wt%) were prepared via vacuum induction melting under a high-purity Ar atmosphere.
Hot-forged into rods with a diameter of 16.5 mm.
Solution treatment at 1050 °C for 2 h to achieve a microstructure with nearly equiaxed grains; this treatment is applied to all four steels, hereafter referred to as 4Al, 6Al, 8Al and 10Al.

processing_steps.cooling_medium: oil (b0016); specimens described as machined from 'water-quenched steel rods' in b0022
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Quenching after the 1050 °C/2 h solution treatment; b0016 says oil quenching, b0022 says tensile specimens were machined from water-quenched steel rods.

structures.overall_structure: Single-phase face-centered cubic (FCC) γ austenite lightweight steel with quasi-equiaxed grains; the austenite grains contain numerous annealing twin boundaries.
After tensile deformation the 4Al austenite is characterized by dislocation cell blocks, which is common in low-carbon or low-aluminum lightweight steels.

unmapped_findings: The 4Al (Fe-35Mn-4Al-0.1C) steel is described as an austenitic lightweight steel (single-phase FCC austenite), distinct from the 6Al (austenite-based duplex), 8Al and 10Al (ferrite-based duplex) steels [b0014, b0025].

Measured composition of the 4Al steel by wet-chemical analysis (Table 1, wt%): Mn 33.92, Al 4.13, C 0.094, Nb 0.11, V 0.11, Mo 1.20, W 0.98, Fe Bal. Only bulk 4Al composition is reported (no separate 4Al_γ/4Al_α rows in Table 1). [b0018]

The nominal composition in the Materials section is given as Fe-35Mn-xAl-1C-0.1Nb-0.1V-1Mo-1W (x = 4 wt%) [b0016], while the title/abstract use Fe-35Mn-xAl-0.1C; the measured C for 4Al is 0.094 wt% [b0018].

By SADP along the [100]γ zone axis, satellite diffraction spots near the γ reflections (related to Al and C concentration fluctuations / spinodal decomposition during quenching) are seen in all four steels and their intensity decreases with increasing Al content; for the 4Al austenite no {110} SRO/L1₂-type superlattice spot is circled in the SADP (Fig. 1e), unlike the 6Al-10Al steels [b0026, figure_001].
As tensile deformation proceeds for 4Al steel, the austenite microhardness increases with increasing strain [b0038, figure_003].

The 4Al steel exhibits typical three-stage strain hardening (stages A, D and E), in contrast to the 8Al steel's five-stage behavior, suggesting a different deformation mechanism [b0038, b0070, figure_003].
The stacking-fault energy of the 4Al austenite is 51.25 mJ·m^-2 at 23 °C (lowest of the four steels; increases to 62.64 for 6Al and 68.47 for 8Al) [table_002, b0029].
The density of the 4Al steel is 7.42 g cm^-3 (highest of the four steels: 7.42, 7.18, 6.99 and 6.84 g cm^-3 for 4Al, 6Al, 8Al, 10Al respectively) [b0016].
